items.text: The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC). Police at every level use the database for warrants, missing persons, criminal histories, stolen property and background checks. CNN reported it first, and the AP and NBC confirmed it through people familiar with the matter. The FBI declined to comment and the scope is not yet clear. In a Fox News interview on Saturday Trump said the administration had just heard about it and that it is 'not good', though he also suggested it could be given 'a positive spin'. If confirmed, this is the FBI's second major breach this year, after the September ShinyHunters claim. It also follows a run of federal outages (the FAA ground stop and NSANet) that officials blamed on routine upgrades.
items.notes: Based on anonymous sources (CNN, NBC, AP). The FBI has not confirmed and Director Patel has not commented. Al Jazeera dates the first reports to Friday Nov 20 and Trump's comment to Saturday Nov 21. Some outlets suggested a link to a Russia probe ('Russia hoax' remark), but the AP says there is no sign of a link to the earlier outages.

items.text: The Agriculture Department is dealing with a security incident that its cyber operations centre found last week. According to internal emails seen by Nextgov/FCW, IT staff reset every database password across all environments, which took many applications offline for several days. Affected systems include payment tools for farmers (crop insurance and loss-coverage programmes), client portals for loan and aid status, and some staff VPN access. On Nov 21 NBC described it as an apparent cyberattack, and farm-trade outlets cite claims that Russian-speaking hackers were involved. Nextgov says it is unclear who was behind the intrusion or whether data was taken.
items.notes: Nextgov first reported this on Nov 19 and NBC's 'cyberattack' report came on Nov 21 (via Al Jazeera). The Russian-speaking-hacker attribution is unverified (AgWeb 'allegedly'). USDA and CISA have not commented on the record.

items.text: Trump told Fox News that he hopes Iran tries to run the US blockade of its ports with a reported 14-tanker convoy from Kharg Island, and that the ships would sink 'like the rest of the navy'. On Sunday the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre reported an incident in the Gulf of Oman involving a tanker and military forces. It did not name the vessel or link it to the convoy. Maritime-sanctions expert Charlie Brown (UANI) called the convoy plan likely propaganda, saying satellite images show no significant loading at Kharg, while ISW warned that an attempt could come within days. CENTCOM said on Nov 18 that ships taking Iranian cargo through ship-to-ship transfers may also be seized.
items.notes: The convoy is reported only by Iranian outlet Hamshahri and Euronews and has not been confirmed. The UKMTO incident is not linked to it. Fox leans right; Al Jazeera is a counterweight on the blockade's reach. A Newsmax headline (Nov 22) says Trump claimed Iran's weekly missile and drone attacks hit a high, but the article could not be read.

items.text: US District Judge Mary McElroy in Providence ruled that HUD unlawfully tried to remake the Continuum of Care homelessness programme, which has more than $4bn in FY2026 funding. HUD planned to set aside $1.3bn for transitional housing and service-only grants, moving away from the housing-first model. She found HUD exceeded its authority under the McKinney-Vento Act by adding criteria that bypass reviews of existing projects' performance. She also struck down a ban on grantee activities aimed at drug users, such as needle exchanges, and a rule letting HUD disqualify applicants that do not promote 'self-sufficiency'. HUD must let applicants amend and resubmit through Dec 1 and award funds by Dec 31. The plaintiffs are 22 mostly Democratic-led states, DC and advocacy groups.
items.notes: Late catch from Nov 20, not logged before. This is a renewed challenge, on different grounds, after an appeals court lifted McElroy's earlier injunction. HUD did not comment and an appeal is likely. The Epoch Times (right-leaning) also covers it as 'key parts' blocked.

items.text: US District Judge Trina Thompson in San Francisco ruled that Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins violated the First Amendment's establishment clause with religious messages sent from her official email to USDA's roughly 100,000 employees. She pointed to Rollins's authority over staff and to wording that presented Christianity as a shared faith. Rollins must stop proselytizing staff, stop when asked and not use her position to pressure subordinates. She may still talk about her faith and politely invite colleagues to religious events. Six employees and the National Federation of Federal Employees brought the suit in May, and USDA says it is considering an appeal.
items.notes: Late catch, not logged before. The roundup dates it Nov 20, while La Nación (wire) says Thursday Nov 19.

items.text: US District Judge William Young in Massachusetts reportedly ruled unconstitutional the administration's transgender-related conditions on Ryan White HIV/AIDS programme grants. The conditions required grantees to comply with administration orders on gender identity in order to receive funding. Details of the remedy were not available in the source found.
items.notes: Single, less-established roundup. Needs confirmation from a wire or court docket before it gets prominent use. Late catch (Nov 19).

items.text: The Federal Communications Commission voted on Thursday to bar China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom and other covered IP-enabled providers from direct access to US telephone numbers. It cited national security and the need to curb scam robocalls. The three carriers were already barred from providing international telecom services to the US. Weekend headlines say Beijing vowed to defend its companies' interests.
items.notes: The vote date is inferred: SCMP says 'Thursday' and its image path is dated Nov 20. The Chinese reaction comes only from a headline in a Nov 22 digest and was not read in full. The FCC order text was not checked.

items.text: On Sunday evening the Lublin District Prosecutor's Office said debris from Kh-101 cruise missiles had been found at all three sites hit on Nov 20: Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik nad Sanem and Mołodycz. Officials had at first described the Mołodycz object as a probable jet drone. Preliminary findings say all three missiles were made in Russia in the fourth quarter of 2026 at plants in Dubna, Moscow Oblast, and WP reports that the Biłgoraj missile was built in October. Site work at Rudnik and Nowy Lipowiec has ended and is continuing at Mołodycz, where fragments fell around fish ponds. Military counterintelligence (SKW) is analysing recovered electronics, and the evidence will go to lab and expert testing.
items.thread: Russian missiles and drones over Poland
items.notes: Gazeta Wyborcza first reported it, citing unofficial information, and the Lublin prosecutors then confirmed it. This corrects the earlier official account of two missiles and a drone (E-261121-16). Euronews says 'plants in Dubna' and WP says 'a plant'. Prosecutors say only written expert opinions will be binding.

items.text: The North Atlantic Council meets in extraordinary session at ambassador level in Brussels on Monday, at Poland's request, after Russian missiles entered Polish airspace. Deputy Defence Minister Paweł Zalewski represents Poland. He is joined by Brig. Gen. Jarosław Stróżyk, head of Military Counterintelligence, who will brief allies on the missiles and on Russian threats. Zalewski told Polsat News that Poland wants stronger air defence for the eastern flank, including AWACS surveillance aircraft and other air assets, and wants NATO's rules sped up so pilots can decide faster whether to shoot down threatening objects. Poland is not invoking Article 4. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte is due to speak after the meeting.
items.thread: Russian missiles and drones over Poland
items.notes: This is a preview: the meeting's outcome was not known at the time of writing. RMF24 says Kosiniak-Kamysz earlier asked for AWACS and allied F-35 support. Zalewski declined to go beyond what the government had already disclosed.

items.text: Deputy Digital Affairs Minister Paweł Olszewski said on Sunday that the ministry's disinformation centre was tracking a wave of Russian false claims tied to reports of a Ukrainian drone attack on Kaliningrad oblast. He named claims that Poland and Lithuania joined Ukraine in attacking Russia, that German troops in Poland coordinated the strike, and that NATO attacked Kaliningrad. He urged people to rely on official sources. On Saturday a Ukrainian Telegram channel reported explosions near the Baltic Fleet base in Baltiysk, which has not been independently confirmed. Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys denied any involvement and said Lithuania had not authorised use of its airspace.
items.notes: The Kaliningrad strike itself is unconfirmed, and the governor spoke only of a 'suspicious object' (GSC summary). PAP carried the same item, but its page could not be fetched.

items.text: Radio Kraków has added detail on the shrunken Clean Transport Zone (SCT) that goes out for consultation on 27 November. Krzysztof Wojdowski of the city roads authority ZDMK said residents paying income or agricultural tax in Kraków would no longer need to be registered (meldunek) in the city to get the exemption. The exemption would cover non-compliant cars bought, rented or leased by 31 December 2028 and would last as long as the resident keeps the car. The zone would follow the first ring road, plus Piłsudskiego, Zwierzyniecka and al. Krasińskiego on the western side. Boundary streets would be inside the zone. Comments can be sent from 27 November to 18 December, online or at ZDMK, ul. Centralna 53. The mayor says the rules could take effect in February or March 2027.
items.notes: The 31 Dec 2028 vehicle-acquisition cut-off appears new compared with earlier coverage. The official consultation form is not yet online (from 27 Nov).

items.text: Ahead of the Main Square Christmas market (27 Nov–1 Jan), the city is discussing extra safeguards with the city police commander, and more police and municipal guard patrols may appear on the square. Temporary barriers put up at the square's entrances after the 7 November attack will stay for now. Mayor Gibała said they are neither attractive nor very functional. Retractable bollards are planned at all entrances in 2027. The city has set money aside in the budget, and the voivode has reportedly agreed to co-finance them. A separate fair on Mały Rynek, run by the IMAGO folk art centre, runs from 30 November to 3 January. Gibała said it is not yet decided whether future markets go to tender or are run by the city.
items.notes: Voivode co-financing is reported ('reportedly agreed'), not confirmed by the voivode's office. Mały Rynek end date is 3 Jan here; earlier coverage gave only the 30 Nov opening.

items.text: Prosecutors investigating the 7 November attack want to question the psychologist and doctors who examined the attacker when he applied for a sports-firearms permit, Rzeczpospolita reports. Eryk Stasielak of the National Prosecutor's Office in Kraków said questioning the psychologist needs a prosecutor's decision lifting professional secrecy, while the doctors need a court ruling lifting medical secrecy. He said a motion to the court is being prepared, covering every member of the team that issued the opinion. According to the paper, the Police Internal Affairs Bureau will also examine how the permit was granted. Interia adds that the permit was valid from January and the first gun was bought on 6 March. No motive has been stated.
items.notes: Interia shows no publication date (page cached 23 Nov). It probably dates from 21–22 Nov and may overlap the PAP item of 20 Nov already logged. Interia says four firearms (two AR-15s, two pistols) were in the car, while PAP (E-261121-26) said two were registered. These can both be true but are unreconciled.

items.text: Prof. Andrzej Szarata, rector of Kraków University of Technology and chair of the city's Council for the Construction of the Metro, says the mayor halted metro preparations without consulting the council, which still formally exists. In an Interia interview he said Kraków ranked second after Warsaw for metro readiness in a report by the Centre for EU Transport Projects (CUPT). He warned that stopping the geological drilling tender and the feasibility study, which EU funding requires, could cost two to three years. He said the council will send Gibała a position paper summarising two years of work, and urged him to ask Prime Minister Tusk for a concrete funding commitment. He welcomed Deputy PM Kosiniak-Kamysz's support and questioned the city's switch to seven new tram routes, citing limited tram and bus capacity.
items.notes: Publication date not shown (page cached 23 Nov); probably 20–22 Nov. Interview, one-sided. City Hall has not responded in this piece. The extraordinary council session is on 25 Nov at 16:00.

items.text: About 80% of the trees marked for felling at Fort 'Za Rzeką' on ul. Rydla in Bronowice have been cut, according to the University of the National Education Commission (UKEN), which is building a shooting range complex there. Media put the total at about 270 trees, and residents say nearly 300. The project uses the 7 July 2023 special act on university shooting ranges. The voivode issued the permit on 21 October with immediate enforceability, so work began before any appeals were heard. Residents say they are not parties to the proceedings. 376 people signed a petition to the voivode and 263 students petitioned the rector. They also point to hollows of protected woodpeckers. The university told Dziennik Polski that a dendrologist checked every tree, that it will plant at least as many replacements, and that the range will be finished by the end of 2027.
items.notes: University position via Dziennik Polski (19 Nov). Krakowski Raport has asked the voivode why immediate enforceability was granted and how many appeals were filed, with no answer yet. Krakowski Raport is a Watch source.

items.text: A woman of about 60 riding a bicycle was hit by a car in Gdów (Wieliczka county) at 7:52 on Sunday and died at the scene. Three fire crews and an LPR air ambulance were sent. Fire service spokesman Hubert Ciepły told TVN24 that more than 15 firefighters worked with medical crews. The road was closed at the scene, with detours in place.
items.notes: Aggregated report; original TVN24 piece not read.

items.text: Fire broke out around noon on Sunday in an apartment block on ul. Świętokrzyska in Kęty, Oświęcim county. Residents were evacuated. According to Gazeta Krakowska, some people were injured and taken to hospital, condition unknown. Two LPR helicopters landed at the scene and the road was fully closed. The cause is under investigation.
items.outlet: Krakowski Raport (citing Gazeta Krakowska, Onet Kraków)
items.notes: Number of injured not given.

items.text: Kraków is consulting its draft county programme for people with disabilities for 2027–2030. Consultations began on 13 November. An open meeting is held on Monday 23 November, 17:00–19:00, at the Zabłocie social innovation cluster. Comments can be sent until 4 December by email (sz.umk@um.krakow.pl) or e-Doręczenia marked 'KONSULTACJE PPD'. The draft and form are on BIP.

Researchers at Kraków University of Technology, led by Dr Julia Radwan-Pragłowska, have developed a sponge that stops heavy bleeding when pressed onto a wound. It needs no special skills to use. Unlike many products that use crustacean-derived chitosan, it is made only from non-animal materials. Its very porous structure absorbs blood and promotes clotting. Patent applications have been filed in Poland and internationally, a US filing is being prepared, and production from domestic raw materials is planned.
items.notes: Developer's claims; no independent clinical data cited.

items.text: Kraków is marking what would have been Krzysztof Penderecki's 93rd birthday on 23 November with three concerts in the Philharmonic hall. The Philharmonic performed Credo on 21 November and Sinfonietta Cracovia played on 22 November in memory of Elżbieta and Krzysztof Penderecki. On 23 November at 19:00 Sinfonia Iuventus, conducted by Jurek Dybał, plays with cellist Arto Noras. Orchestras in Amsterdam, Boston, Bonn, Dresden, Zagreb, Lviv and Paris are also marking the anniversary.

Public transport authority ZTP is boosting night service for Andrzejki parties. On the night of 26–27 November, bus 611 runs three times an hour from about 23:30 to 2:00. On the nights of 27–28 and 29–30 November, trams 62 and 69 use larger vehicles. Temporary night buses 604 (Prądnik Biały–Swoszowice SKA) and 618 (Kliny–Rondo Kocmyrzowskie) run hourly. Buses 605 and 611 run every 15 minutes, and 664 every 15 minutes until about 3:30.
items.notes: Published 20 Nov, not found in the logged events; included as a practical item for this week.

items.text: Winter has reached Małopolska. Radio Kraków forecast snowfall across the region overnight into Monday 23 November, with about -1°C in Kraków and -5°C in Zakopane. IMGW forecasts reported by RMF24 give daytime highs of about 1–4°C early in the week. Some places may stay below zero on Thursday and Friday, with frosts of several degrees at night and down to about -10°C in the mountains, and a risk of icy roads. Twojapogoda expects frost day and night in the south by the weekend. No IMGW warning for Małopolska was reported in the sources checked.
items.notes: IMGW warnings were not checked directly on meteo.imgw.pl. Longer-range figures (down to -15°C or -20°C) come from Twojapogoda, a commercial forecaster.

items.text: An update to CoWKrakowie's report on the line 15 derailment on ul. Kamienna on 20 November says trams were running again by 7:11 that morning, after the car was put back on the track. The earlier entry had no reopening time. No cause has been given.
items.notes: This is a correction to E-261121-35.

items.text: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah arrived in New Delhi on Nov 22 for a two-day state visit and was received by MoS Jitin Prasada. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar called on him that evening at his hotel; Nepali outlet Khabarhub says they covered connectivity, trade, transit, energy, education and people-to-people ties. The Nov 23 programme includes a Rashtrapati Bhavan reception, delegation talks with Modi at Hyderabad House, an exchange of MoUs, a joint press statement, a call on President Murmu, and the expected unveiling of a 'Samriddha Nepal, Samunnat Bharat' joint vision document. Nepali media also expect the two leaders to lay the foundation stone of the 669 MW Lower Arun hydropower project by video and flag off a weekly Janakpur–Ayodhya train. Reports of the size of an Indian aid package vary from about USD 1.5 billion (Khabarhub) to a USD 2 billion Nepali request (The Open Press). Nepal is still pressing for extra air entry routes.
items.notes: Outcomes not yet reported at time of writing. The aid figures are unofficial and conflict across outlets. Dainik Jagran (Nov 22) cites sources dismissing reports that Nepal's airports would be raised. The Jaishankar call is reported by Khabarhub and Times Now Navbharat.

items.text: Tamil Nadu's HR&CE Commissioner has filed a petition asking the Supreme Court to review its Nov 20 interim order, which allows a one-time lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon pillar on Thiruparankundram hill on Nov 24, LawBeat reports. The state and the temple administration argue that by custom the lamp is lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchi Pillaiyar temple, and they warn of law-and-order risks. On Nov 22 a federation of Muslim organisations welcomed the review: it says it does not oppose the lamp itself, only the change of site, and the Waqf Board has engaged senior counsel (The News Minute). The main appeals are listed for January 2027, and it was not clear whether the review would be heard before the festival.
items.notes: Contested story. The right-leaning Organiser (Nov 22) presents the review as a TVK government play for minority votes, quotes BJP-linked critics and says a stay is unlikely. The News Minute foregrounds Muslim groups' argument from custom and BJP leader H Raja's 'Ayodhya of South' remark. The News Minute says the review was expected to be heard Nov 23, which we could not confirm. ANI earlier reported that the dargah side also planned a review.

items.text: Citing an unnamed official quoted by Business Standard, Swarajya reports that India and the EU are set to sign their free trade agreement in Brussels on Dec 16, during PM Modi's visit. The European Commission has sent the Council of the EU proposals for approval to sign and conclude the deal, including the final legal text and tariff schedules. EU Ambassador Jean-Eric Paquet said the pact would take effect next year. The Dec 16 date was first reported in September; the new step is the Commission's referral to the Council.
items.notes: Signing date rests on an unnamed official. The Indian domestic approval steps were not described.

items.text: Nagpur district has started a fresh verification drive for voters flagged as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate during the Special Intensive Revision, The Live Nagpur reports. The drive covers 14.43 lakh entries across 12 assembly seats: 2.40 lakh reported dead, 5.46 lakh absent, 5.30 lakh shifted and about 9,500 other. About 1.18 lakh had already completed enrolment. Voters can file declarations online or through the ECINET app. Forms run until Nov 30, claims and objections until Dec 15, and final rolls are due Dec 22.
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: Local outlet; figures are district-level. No statewide restoration count yet.

items.text: BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute of Maharashtra died of cardiac arrest at AIIMS New Delhi late on Nov 21, aged 72, according to news roundups. He was admitted on Nov 20, had been elected to the Rajya Sabha in April 2026, and served in the Maharashtra Legislative Council from 2014 to 2019. PM Modi expressed condolences. His death leaves a Rajya Sabha vacancy from Maharashtra.
items.notes: Based only on two daily roundups; not checked against a wire report.

items.text: Two Army soldiers, Naik Manish Kumar and Naik Ankush Kumar, died on Nov 22 when a tank ran over them during training near Bhojraj village in Hisar, Haryana, Times Now Navbharat reports. According to police, dust cut the driver's visibility. No Army statement had been reported.
items.notes: Live-blog item only.

items.text: Times Now Navbharat, citing unnamed sources, reports that the BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal may revive their alliance in Punjab, with a formal announcement possible next week. Seat-sharing is said to be still under discussion, and BJP leaders may visit Punjab shortly. Neither party has confirmed the report.
items.notes: Attributed only to sources; treat as speculation until announced.

items.text: In Itanagar on Nov 22, Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah launched Arunachal Pradesh initiatives worth ₹5,610.95 crore, including Mission Shikshit Arunachal Phase II (₹1,500 crore). He also opened the NDRF 12th Battalion campus, which will train state disaster response forces for all eight northeastern states, and released the Arunachal Pradesh Cooperative Vision 2047. He advised the Army and ITBP to buy farm produce directly from local farmers through cooperatives.
items.notes: Confirms the scheduled event happened. Source is a digest drawing on PIB; we did not open the PIB original.

items.text: The first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum ended in New Delhi on Nov 22 with the adoption of an 'Indraprastha Communiqué'. A current-affairs digest drawing on official releases gives attendance as 116 delegates from 22 countries. The communiqué's full text was not reviewed.
items.notes: Earlier reporting said about 25 countries were invited; 22 attended per this digest.

items.text: Several deadly road crashes were reported on Nov 21–22. Nine members of a family from Dhule, Maharashtra, returning from Khatu Shyamji, died when their vehicle hit a parked truck on the Kota–Udaipur highway near Shambhupura in Rajasthan. Seven people died in Kutch, Gujarat, when a car hit a trailer, and three died near Phalodi in Rajasthan. PM Modi announced ₹2 lakh ex gratia for the Kutch victims.
items.notes: Roundup sources only; casualty figures may change.

items.text: Democratic Senators Jeanne Shaheen and Chris Coons issued a joint statement condemning Russia for the recent airspace incursions into US allies, including Poland, which they described as a test of Western resolve and an attempt to weaken support for Ukraine. They said the United States should respond immediately. They also criticised President Trump's friendly tone toward Putin at the Shenzhen meeting, arguing it had emboldened rather than restrained him, and pledged that Congress would stand by US allies and Ukraine. The statement was first reported by The Hill.
items.notes: Late catch from Nov 21, not in recent events. Opposition (Democratic) view; contrasts with the administration, which has made no formal statement. Original Hill article not read directly.

items.text: On Saturday Trump posted a series of photos from his China trip on Truth Social, including one with Vladimir Putin captioned 'My friend' and a composite setting a Putin–Xi–Trump picture beside the Stalin–Roosevelt–Churchill wartime photo under the caption 'Great Powers 1945, 2026'. Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev reposted the Putin image. A day earlier in Washington, Trump said Putin had clearly expressed a wish to end the war, that a deal was likely and that his personal relationship with Putin was fantastic. The posts follow Tusk's Nov 19 rebuke of Trump's 'friend' remark; no Polish government reaction to the new posts was reported.
items.notes: Posts described by Polsat; Truth Social originals not viewed. The Big Three photo the caption refers to is from Tehran 1943 (or Yalta 1945), so the caption's date is ambiguous. TVN24 carries Trump's remarks about Putin wanting peace. Byline attribution on the Polsat page is unclear.
